title: Attempt on Metropolis relaxation for geometric-time Cayley targets
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Metropolis relaxation for geometric-time Cayley targets explicit structural calculation Result: Monotone decrease is false already on the two-element Cayley group, with relaxation defined by1/(1-lambda_2). For the nonlazy base walk that flips states, mu_p=(1/(2-p),(1-p)/(2-p)), and its Metropolis matrix is[[p,1-p],[1,0]]. Its second eigenvalue is p-1, hence tau(p)=1/(2-p), which is strictly increasing. The same conclusion survives a lazy base walk: the base matrix has all entries1/2, mu_p=((1+p)/2,(1-p)/2), the Metropolis off-diagonal rates are(1-p)/(2*(1+p)) and1/2, and tau(p)=1+p. Check: For the flip walk, sum the geometric probabilities over even versus odd times. For the lazy base, X_0 is the identity and X_k is uniform for every k>=1. The nontrivial eigenvalue of a two-state stochastic matrix is1 minus the sum of its off-diagonal probabilities, giving both formulas directly. If laziness is imposed after forming the nonlazy Metropolis kernel, tau becomes2/(2-p), still increasing. Obstruction: The literal monotonicity direction is refuted under the standard spectral-gap relaxation convention, but this does not answer the other universal-bound questions or resolve the source undefined tau(infinity). If relaxation meant inverse absolute gap for a nonlazy chain, that convention differs; the lazy example has nonnegative spectrum and removes that ambiguity. Prior-art status remains unverified.

title: Attempt on Largest growing fork-join batch compatible with asymptotic independence
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A finite-horizon input coupling suggests a cubic collision scale. Fix k tagged servers. Jobs arrive at rate Lambda=lambda*n/k and choose a uniform k-subset. If N is the number of tagged servers hit by an arrival, E[N(N-1)]=k*(k-1)*k*(k-1)/(n*(n-1)). Remove arrivals that hit at least two tagged queues and restore their lost marginal rates by independent Poisson streams. A union bound on removed events and added events is at most (3/2)*Lambda*T*E[N(N-1)], hence at most 3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)). The resulting streams are independent with the correct marginal rates. With independent task marks and queues initially empty, this also bounds total variation of their workload paths on [0,T]. Extending the credited source coupling to stationary starts gives TV<=2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)), where r(T) is the stationary marginal emptying tail. With independent exponential service of rate mu>lambda, a stopped generator calculation gives r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T). Taking T=2*log(n)/(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2 gives sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail r(T)<=C*T^(-p) gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Check: The hypergeometric factorial moment follows by summing ordered pairs of tagged-server indicators. On N>=2, both 1<=N(N-1)/2 and N<=N(N-1), giving the factor 3/2. Small subset enumeration checks the moment exactly. Separate exact checks cover 77 hypergeometric/restoration cases, 81 generator identities, nine geometric exponential moments and five polynomial balancing identities. The complete packet explicitly checks stationary coupling, marginal rate restoration, PASTA and heavy-traffic limits; these are author checks, not independent review. Obstruction: Partial exponential-service sufficient regime only. No optimal threshold, boundary k of order n^(1/3), general-service improvement, correlated-mark result, uniform heavy-traffic result or novelty certification. The basic source coupling is credited.

title: Attempt on Singularity of distinct free and wired forest measures
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Distinct invariant ergodic laws are mutually singular Result: For a fixed countable group action, two distinct invariant ergodic probability measures are mutually singular. In the Lebesgue decomposition of one relative to the other, the absolutely continuous part is invariant. Its density is invariant and hence constant under the second ergodic law; ergodicity of the first forces its absolutely continuous mass to be either zero or one. Nonzero overlap therefore forces equality. Check: The singular and absolutely continuous parts are preserved by the action by uniqueness of Lebesgue decomposition; this is the load-bearing invariance step. Obstruction: This handles forest laws admitting such an ergodic common action. Arbitrary networks may lack it; two distinct probability laws need not be singular in general.

title: Attempt on Variation of nearest-unvisited walk length under a random start
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Variation of nearest-unvisited walk length under a random start structural calculation Result: Let m and M be the minimum and maximum start-dependent lengths, R=M/m. The elementary bound Var(X)<=(M-E X)*(E X-m) implies sd(X)/E X<=(R-1)/(2*sqrt(R)) for any X in[m,M]. Classical nearest-neighbor-tour comparison gives R=O(log n), since every walk length is at least MST length and its length is at most O(log n) times a TSP tour, at most twice MST length. Hence a rigorous O(sqrt(log n)) coefficient-of-variation bound follows, short of an absolute constant. Check: The variance inequality follows by averaging(X-m)*(M-X)>=0. Maximizing(M-u)*(u-m)/u^2 over u in[m,M] gives u=2Mm/(M+m) and the displayed exact ratio. This is sharper than simply bounding standard deviation by the range. Obstruction: The deterministic logarithmic approximation examples do not automatically give a large random-start coefficient of variation. One must also control how many starting vertices exhibit the long route.

title: Attempt on Limit of the normalised log-effective resistance of the DGFF electric network
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Bound log R_eff by the field along an annulus decomposition; compare upper and lower bounds. Result: Rayleigh monotonicity gives R_eff(x, D_N^c) <= sum over dyadic annuli around x of the resistance across the annulus, each bounded by the maximum of e^{beta h} over the annulus times a constant, so log R_eff <= beta max_{annuli} (h max over annulus) summed... more precisely log R_eff <= log sum_k e^{beta M_k} where M_k is the field maximum over annulus k; by the concentric decomposition M_k is the walk value at scale k plus a bounded extremal term, so log R_eff is bounded above by beta times the maximum over k of the concentric walk, which after dividing by (log N)^{1/2} converges to beta sqrt g times the maximum of a Brownian motion on [0,1]. The lower bound via cutsets gives the same functional with the minimum over annuli of the field minimum, i.e. a different functional. The two bounds do not match: the upper bound is a maximum of a Brownian motion and the lower bound is a minimum, so the limit distribution is sandwiched between beta sqrt g times max and min of a Brownian motion but not identified. The notes' guess of a CGFF limit for the field x -> log R_eff is consistent with this sandwich only if the resistance is dominated by the coarse scale. Key identity: beta sqrt g min_{[0,1]} B <= liminf (log N)^{-1/2} log R_eff <= beta sqrt g max_{[0,1]} B in distribution (heuristic sandwich). Obstruction: Upper (flow) and lower (cutset) bounds converge to different functionals of the concentric walk.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0014-limit-of-the-normalised-log-effective-resistance-of-the-dgff-electric

title: Circular Law for the Complex Ginibre Ensemble
body: Let X_n be an n by n random matrix whose entries are independent and identically distributed standard complex Gaussian random variables, meaning each entry has independent real and imaginary parts distributed N(0, 1/2), so that E[|X_{jk}|^2] = 1. Let M_n = X_n / sqrt(n). Then, almost surely, the empirical spectral distribution of the eigenvalues of M_n converges weakly, as n tends to infinity, to the uniform probability distribution on the unit disk {z in C : |z| <= 1}. [Ginibre (1965), Mehta; see Bai and Silverstein, Spectral Analysis of Large Dimensional Random Matrices]

body:

Method: Explicit deterministic shy coupling on an annulus Result: If an isometry F preserves a reflected-Brownian domain and has inf_x |x-F(x)|>0, take Y_t=F(X_t). Orthogonal transformation of Brownian noise and equivariance of inward reflection show Y has the correct reflected law, while separation stays positive. On R<|x|<R_out, F(x)=-x yields |X_t-Y_t|>=2R. title: Attempt on Rate of convergence in the circular law as a function of the moment assumption
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Locate the rate bottleneck in the Hermitisation argument. Result: The Hermitisation proof controls the log-potential U_n(z) = (1/n) log|det(n^{-1/2}M_n - z)| through the singular-value distribution of the shifted matrix; the error has three parts: (a) the rate in the Marchenko-Pastur-type convergence of the singular-value distribution, of order n^{-1/2}-ish under four moments and degrading to n^{-c(eps)} under 2+eps moments through the truncation at level n^{1/(2+eps)}; (b) the smallest singular value lower bound, which contributes only a log-factor to the log-potential error; (c) the conversion from log-potential convergence to weak convergence of the ESD, which costs a power through the smoothing of the Laplacian. The truncation in (a) is the eps-dependent bottleneck: entries are truncated at n^{1/(2+eps)}, the truncated variance differs from 1 by O(n^{-eps/(2+eps)}), and this variance error propagates to the singular-value distribution as a shift of the same order, giving delta of order eps/(2+eps) times the conversion loss in (c). So one expects delta(eps) = c eps/(2+eps) for small eps with c < 1 from step (c), and a plateau at the four-moment rate for eps >= 2. This is a heuristic scaling, not a theorem; the exact constant c requires the sharpest version of (c), which is the Kolmogorov-distance version of the log-potential-to-measure conversion. Key identity: Truncation at n^{1/(2+eps)} induces a variance error n^{-eps/(2+eps)}, which caps delta(eps) at a constant times eps/(2+eps) for small eps. Obstruction: Sharp conversion constant from log-potential to Kolmogorov distance.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0109-rate-of-convergence-in-the-circular-law-as-a-function-of-the-moment-as
